subject: Monthly Vitals standup + escalation plan
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Monthly Vitals standup + escalation plan

Morning team — attaching the March Monthly Vitals (PDF) and calling out the three items I want on leadership radar for QBR prep: 

1) Latency (p95): +18% month-over-month, driven by increased long-context requests from two enterprise customers during peak windows. See trace attached (latency-trace-20270311.png).

2) Cost per 1M tokens: +12% due to more tail calls and model fallback to larger variants on cold starts. We need concrete batching and caching mitigations.

3) Uptime blip: 2027-03-11 02:14 UTC — ~22m of partial degradation affecting some EU routes; automatic fallback worked but we had higher error rates for embeddings.

Usage continues to climb (15% month-over-month), which is great, but it amplifies the two issues above. For QBR I want: concise one-slide root-cause + current mitigation, an owner for each bullet, and a short escalation plan if we see another 10% p95 regression in the next 14 days.

Asks (today/tomorrow):
- Jonas: can you confirm ownership for the standby routing policy tweak and whether we can throttle a single noisy tenant?
- Marcus: please surface the top-3 longest traces and attach any kernel-level notes.
- Tessa: cost playbook — are we ready to push a temporary quantization profile and what impact do you expect?
- Laura: I'd appreciate a 1-paragraph note for execs summarizing business impact for Acme Corp (they were affected during the uptime blip).

Proposed escalation (if p95 +10% again): brief exec note, soft credit for affected customers, and a canary that pins critical accounts to Dedicated for 48 hours while we stabilize.

Drive dash: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-monthly-vitals-dashboard
Jira SUP-3421 tracks the EU partial outage.

Attachments: 2027-03-Monthly-Vitals.pdf; latency-trace-20270311.png

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Director, Customer Reliability 
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:15:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Monthly Vitals standup + escalation plan

Thanks Aisha — quick updates inline.

- Standby routing / noisy tenant: I can enable a per-tenant soft rate limit for the traffic pattern we saw. That should blunt the p95 tail within the hour for requests routed through us. I'm opening SUP-3430 to track the change (low-risk toggle). Owner: Jonas Weber.

- EU outage: we traced the partial degradation to a misrouted autoscaler event between two AZs; root cause already in SUP-3421. Marcus, can you prioritize the three longest traces Steve flagged in the attached dashboard? I pasted a direct link to the trace collection in Drive.

- Cost mitigation: Tessa, agree that a temporary quant profile (Q4) plus a short KV-cache warmup policy should reduce fallback to larger variants. If you can provide an estimate of cost delta by EOD we can include it in the exec note.

Drive quick link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-monthly-vitals-dashboard (see "Traces / March 11")

Jonas

Excellent summary, Aisha. Two leadership-level points: 

1) Communications & commercial risk: Acme Corp saw increased error surface during the EU blip. Sam Wu from Acme (cc'd by Aisha on the ticket) will need a short exec note by EOD today outlining impact and remediation steps. Can someone draft a 3-line statement I can sign off?

2) Capacity levers: I'm supportive of the short Dedicated pin for critical accounts as a mitigation test. Finance will want a projected delta; Marcus/Tessa please include a 48-hour cost estimate. We should only do this for customers whose SLA risk is material.

Also, for QBR I want a single slide with: 1-line summary, top-3 indicators (p95, cost/1M, availability), and two short actions (owner + ETA). Jonas — can we get that by COB Monday?

Adding the operational plan and short-term artifacts.

1) Traces: top-3 traces attached (latency-trace-20270311.png) and linked in Drive — root cause pinned to misrouted autoscaler handoff + hot-spot on KV-store leading to cold starts. I annotated the traces with kernel selection notes; early evidence suggests one model variant fell back to a less-quantized kernel under memory pressure.

2) Actions (owners + ETA):
- Jonas: enable per-tenant soft limit and monitor p95 for 24h (in progress) — ETA: 3h.
- Marcus: deploy a targeted KV warmup for affected contexts + optimize kernel selection override (manual) — ETA: 24h.
- Tessa: push Q4 quant profile to canary (non-prod to start) and provide 48h cost delta for Dedicated pin — ETA: EOD Monday.
- Laura: draft exec note for Acme once we have cost delta and customer impact lines — ETA: EOD today.

3) Escalation plan (if p95 +10% in 14d):
- Immediate: open a customer-facing incident summary + offer a pro-rated credit.
- T+2h: pin affected tenant to Dedicated for 48h while kernel/kv mitigations run.
- T+24h: if still unstable, route through fallback regional cluster with higher headroom and alert sales for account outreach.

I scheduled a 30-minute standup at 09:00 PT Monday to validate metrics and confirm the QBR slide. Invite: Jonas, Tessa, Aisha, Laura. Calendar link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=monthly-vitals-standup

Attachments: latency-trace-20270311.png

Marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
